_readme: William's decisions from import-report.md. warband_aliases: a source warband name -> type slugs ([] leaves it out); MiM restrictions use them too; one that keeps the mapping the build would make reads as settled in the report. extra_warband_types: warbands neither Broheim nor mordheimer lists. group_members: add/remove type slugs per group slug, and keep_in/keep_out the types William keeps in or out of a group (held there); each settles its types' group questions. setting_grades: setting slug -> grade. keep_hidden_items: mordheimer items it hides that should be imported anyway. drop_items: mordheimer items left out. item_warbands: item name -> the only type slugs that may buy it, and why. item_warbands_add: item name -> type slugs added to its mordheimer list, and why. item_exclusions: item name -> the only type slugs an item for everyone shuts out, and why. item_defaults_kept: item name -> why the default its contradictions took stands. item_notes: item name -> a soft note added to each of its price rows. whole_names: names matched as a whole on the same-name list, not split at the slash. setting_assignments: kind (skills, hired_swords, dramatis_personae) -> our row's name as the report shows it ("Sniper (Hochland Bandits)") -> setting slug (one mordheimer gives several settings is then settled). skill_lists: a skill list's name -> who learns the skills of it mordheimer lacks (for_everyone, or warbands as {type} or {group} slugs), large_only (a Large unit's skill) and a note shown when learning. drop_skills: our skill rows left out (label -> why). extra_skills: skill rows our table lacks. skill_descriptions: a skill row's description put right (label -> text).
